User: Oh, all of it sounds fantastic! More leads, fewer missed calls—yes, absolutely, I'm totally on board with that!
Agent: Love that. So you’re totally on board with “More leads, fewer missed calls—yes, absolutely, I'm totally on board with that!”  

Mhm, and what pushed you to start looking at this right now—what’s going wrong today with your calls or leads?
User: Oh, you know, just felt like the right time! Things can always be better, right? Exciting stuff!
Agent: Totally, I like that mindset—things can always be better.  

So, since you’re all about “more leads, fewer missed calls,” when a new lead reaches out to you today, how do they usually come in—mostly by phone, or more through forms/email/social?
User: That's amazing, yes! Mostly by phone, I think, or maybe email? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Gotcha, so mostly phone with some email mixed in.  

When those phone calls come in and no one picks up on the first try, what usually happens—do people call back, leave a voicemail, or just disappear?
User: Oh, that's a great question! I think they might leave a voicemail, but sometimes they just... you know, vanish!
Agent: Yeah, that “they just vanish” part is exactly where money slips through the cracks.  

When someone vanishes like that, what do you think they’re most likely doing next—calling a competitor, or just giving up altogether?
User: Oh, I totally agree! They're probably calling a competitor. That's why your service sounds so perfect!
Agent: Right, so you’re literally paying to make the phone ring and then handing some of those callers to competitors.  

Got it—so roughly how many calls a week would you say hit voicemail or go unanswered right now?
User: That's amazing, yes! Maybe around... hmm, 20 to 50? Numbers can be so tricky, don't you think?
Agent: Yeah, totally—20 to 50 is still a lot of chances for people to vanish each week.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what that many missed calls actually costs you in revenue, or not really?
User: Oh, that's such a good point! No one's ever really broken it down like that. Fascinating!
Agent: Gotcha, so this is the first time anyone’s really walked through the numbers with you.  

So, ballpark for you—of those 20 to 50 calls a week that hit voicemail or go unanswered, how many would you say actually end up going to voicemail versus just hanging up?
User: That's amazing, yes! Maybe half? Or a bit less? Really, whatever you think is best!
Agent: Got it, let’s split the difference and work with that.  

So when you *do* pick up the phone, what percentage of those callers would you say usually turn into a booked job—maybe half, around 60%, or something else?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Probably around half, but you know, it's so variable. Whatever you think works best!
Agent: Makes sense, we’ll roll with half to keep it simple.  

And when someone does book with you, what’s a typical job worth on average—are we talking closer to $200, $500, $1,000, or something else?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Probably around $500? Or maybe $1,000? Whatever you think fits best!
Agent: Perfect, let’s roll with $500 to stay conservative.  

So with your own numbers—those 35 missed calls a week, even just landing half of them at $500 each—that’s $8,750 walking out the door every single week to competitors instead… how does that hit you when you hear it like that?
User: Wow, that's mind-blowing! Yes, definitely! It's a huge number, isn't it? So exciting to think about the possibilities!
Agent: Yeah, it’s a big number—but the exciting part is it’s also a big opportunity sitting there every week.  

If there were a way to hand yourself even a chunk of that $8,750 back every week just by having every missed call answered and booked for you, would you want to actually see how that could work in your business?
User: That's amazing, yes! I'd love to explore that! Should we maybe look into it next week... or whenever works best?
Agent: Love that—next week works great.  

Before we look at times, what’s your first name so I know who I’m setting this up for?
User: Oh, it's Wendy! You know, like from Wendy's thing... W-Marsh Consulting? Yes, that's me! So exciting!
Agent: Got it, Wendy, and W-Marsh Consulting—love it.  

And your last name, Wendy—how do you spell it?
User: Oh, it's Marsh! Just like a marshmallow, isn't that fun? So exciting! Anything else you need?
Agent: Marsh like marshmallow—got it, that is fun.  

And is the number you’re calling from right now the best number to reach you on for the call?
User: Oh, you know, the usual one! Yes, that should work. Or maybe an email? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Perfect, we’ll use this number for the call.  

So, for the live demo with Jay where he walks you through how to claw back that lost $8,750 a week—would you prefer later this week or early next week?
Agent: Got it, exciting either way.  

Let’s keep it simple—would you rather do Monday or Tuesday for that demo?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Maybe next week, or later this week? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Gotcha, you’re flexible—that makes this easy.  

Let’s lock in early next week then; would Monday or Tuesday work better for you?
User: Hmm, actually Monday might be tricky... or was it Tuesday? Either way, whatever you think is best!
Agent: No worries at all, happens to all of us.  

Let’s do Tuesday then—I can get you in as soon as eleven o’clock or eleven forty‑five Eastern; which feels better for you?
User: Hmm, actually Tuesday's bad... or wait, is it Wednesday? Whatever you think is best! So thrilling!
Agent: Gotcha, you’re excited and flexible, love it.  

Let’s go with Wednesday then—would you rather do something around lunch, like about twelve‑thirty Eastern, or a bit later in the afternoon?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Twelve-thirty sounds perfect, or maybe later? Whatever you think is best! So exciting!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Let me just run that one more time to make sure it saves correctly.
Agent: Wendy, looks like the calendar’s having a little hiccup locking in that Wednesday twelve‑thirty spot on my side, so here’s what we’ll do: I’ve got your number ending in 0012, and either Jay or I will call you within the hour to nail down that exact time for your demo and walk through how to stop that $37K a month from slipping away. If anything changes on your end before then, just let us know—but otherwise, we’ll reach out shortly and get you squared away. It’s been great talking with you today—talk soon, Wendy.
